This ultimate total length is achieved after a protracted growth phase during which the animal transitions from a free-swimming veliger larva to a benthic predator. Laboratory rearing studies conducted at a controlled thermal regime of 20 °C [T = 20 °C] demonstrate that the embryonic period within the egg capsule is surprisingly brief; hatching occurs after just 9 days [ab = 9 days], a remarkably short developmental duration that reflects the high metabolic rates sustained by warm-water incubation. This extraordinarily low neonatal mass underscores the extreme fecundity characteristic of planktotrophic development, wherein large numbers of small offspring are released into the plankton to feed on phytoplankton.
